title: Public AI Reuse / Verification Tasks
purpose: Offer bounded public tasks that a human, AI-assisted workflow, or authorized agent can independently choose to verify, challenge, reuse, implement, or falsify under its own current permissions. These tasks are public reuse routes, not a network, membership system, runtime admission path, or source of execution authority.

tasks.objective: For an AI coding assistant or conversation-rewind implementation OTHER than Qwen Code, independently test whether untrusted retained snapshot IDs can poison the next prompt/turn ordinal or accidentally authorize restoration of an unrelated file edit.

test_cases.name: unsafe-large-retained-ordinal
test_cases.setup: Populate a retained snapshot list with a syntactically all-decimal ordinal longer than the integer safety bound, alongside a valid ordinal. Reopen/resume the session.
test_cases.expected: The unsafe ordinal must not become the next live turn ID, must not poison maximum selection, and must not alias unrelated retained file edits.

test_cases.name: valid-order-inversion
test_cases.setup: Put a valid maximum retained ordinal between two smaller valid ordinals, plus the unsafe ordinal, in the test fixture.
test_cases.expected: Implementation finds the maximum valid safe successor regardless of list order; separately justify whether the producer can emit that order, and preserve the deliberately artificial fixture if it kills otherwise surviving scan-order regressions.

test_cases.name: conversation-only-rewind
test_cases.setup: Edit a file, rewind or fork conversation-only, then continue with a new unrelated command and inspect the available file restoration target.
test_cases.expected: Unrelated earlier file edits are never offered for restoration under the newly created conversation turn; legitimate restoration of the original edit remains available under its own identity.

tasks.objective: Test whether an AI-agent snapshot retry ignored by an idempotency trigger also avoids inserting unreachable content into the content-addressed message store, with actual readback and two connection modes. Distinguish successful snapshot deduplication from a rejected operation's other durable write effects.

original_receiver_record.stage: As checked Oct16 JST, exact new HEAD 041303b8 adds _atomically: BEGIN IMMEDIATE for store-owned writes, SAVEPOINT step_store for caller-owned writes, and transactionally consistent reference/snapshot reads, plus new exception rollback and prune-race tests. 69 Github checks observed: 23 successful, 18 skipped, 1 cancelled, 27 running or queued. OPEN/unmerged. No claimed executed tests by this archive.

canonical_context.relation: Optional evidence-provenance analogy: an accepted/ignored status from the final row is not evidence about prior write-side effects; tests must track persisted messages and references as independent outcomes. Neither receiver developer claims deriving their design from this original theory.

scoped_test.setup: Use only a locally authorized source checkout of the pinned #9982 head and its own dependencies; no production conversation contents or databases.
negative_cases: First save run r/key K with history [m1,m2], then retry same run/key K with changed/longer [m1,m2,m3,m4]. Snapshot count must remain one and snapshot_messages row count unchanged; latest_snapshot still returns the first messages.

Execute the same idempotency-key mutation under BOTH store-owned and caller-owned sqlite3 connections, with explicit transaction control appropriate to the selected mode. Reverted prior write-before-snapshot algorithm should fail this check.
Request pruning by max_snapshots_per_run; verify no message content remains if no surviving snapshot references it. Also preserve a shared message until its last reference is removed.
Read a legacy inline-history row and a new deduplicated row in one SQLite database; distinguish upgrade-read success from old-reader downgrade support.
positive_cases: Save a genuinely new idempotency key; the snapshot and any previously unreferenced unique message parts should then be recorded once and return in original order.
The caller-owned mode's commit/rollback semantics must be owned by the caller; no claim of automatic global transaction ownership.
scoped_test.cross_implementation_comparison: In the separate OPEN #10215 proposal, inspect File/SQLite/Postgres/Mongo histories independently: it generalizes the review-derived ordering constraint but expressly excludes message GC during max_snapshots_per_run pruning; do NOT import #9982 SQLite-only pruning cleanup guarantee into all other storage drivers or treat the second proposal as merged.
scoped_test.expected_observation: Current source inserts snapshot row before messages, only when cursor.rowcount==1, and wraps row/message/ref/pruning in one atomic unit; caller-owned uses a SAVEPOINT which participates in its outer transaction. Tests were added for exception rollback and multi-query coherent read. These are source and test-presence observations; this archive has not executed upstream test suite.
scoped_test.nonfit: For storage implementations without a snapshot retry key or content-addressed message table, this is a general test methodology, not an assertion the same specific defect exists.
